name: Dusty violet
lede: Saccardo's Violet is a soft, greyed violet from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color book, most likely named, like its sibling Saccardo's Slate, for the Italian mycologist Pier Andrea Saccardo.

sections.title: A mycologist's color chart
sections.body:
Ridgway drew about 4,000 of his named samples from earlier sources, among them Saccardo's *Chromotaxia*, a chart the Italian mycologist Pier Andrea Saccardo built for naming fungus colors [1]. This violet and [[dark-teal-grey|Saccardo's Slate]] most likely share that source, though no book we hold states the naming directly [1][2].

Ridgway catalogued it on plate XXXVII, hue 61 prime [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In LCH terms it measures lightness 52, chroma 25, hue 315 degrees [3]. Its nearest library neighbors are [[faded-purple|Faded Purple]] and [[pearl-violet|Pearl Violet]], with [[grey-purple|Grey Purple]] close behind [3]. Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds only 3 matches, all in landscapes from the 1850s to 1910s, including Eugène Boudin's 1869 harbor scene *The mole of Deauville* [4]. Saturated violets are rare matches in aged, varnished paintings, where pigments fade and darken unevenly [4].

origin.named_after: most likely Pier Andrea Saccardo, Italian mycologist (1845-1920), author of Chromotaxia
origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature (1912)
